title: openai-resp-v11-proxy: stable streaming, client_seed propagation, and metadata mapper
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Customers adopting the newer OpenAI Responses variants expect two things from our OpenAI-compatibility proxy: (1) streaming stability across fragmented chunks from v11-style responses and (2) transparent propagation of client-provided determinism hints and request metadata. This PR implements a compact proxy layer and mapping rules to preserve the behavior users rely on while avoiding coupling to internal response framing.

What this PR does: implements a responses-v11 compatibility shim that: 1) consolidates streaming fragments into deterministic application events (message/choice/segment) with reassembly metadata so SDKs can rehydrate partial streams without losing token alignment; 2) forwards client-side determinism hints (client_seed and rng_hint) supplied via the OpenAI 'seed' and 'determinism' fields into our internal request context and downstream runtime so that sampling remains reproducible across retries and logs; 3) preserves and exposes user_request_metadata (arbitrary JSON payloads) by mapping them to the x-rw-user-metadata header and including them in response events for auditing and downstream tool calls; 4) adds structured-output attribute mapping so that responses with the new "structured" payload type map to our existing structured-output contract instead of being folded into free-text.

Scope and exclusions: the proxy focuses on behavior required for API compatibility and streaming stability. It does not change model selection or scheduling heuristics; follow-up PRs will add routing policies for quantized model variants that require different seed semantics.

Testing and rollout: included unit tests for chunk reassembly, CI e2e for the streaming path against a synthetic responses-v11 server, and a small perf microbenchmark to verify CPU overhead of the mapper is <2% at typical payload sizes. Rollout will be staged: the feature is behind a feature flag (openai_v11_compat) and will be enabled for a subset of beta customers for one week before broader rollout.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial shim and streaming reassembly; client_seed + metadata passthrough; tests and docs updates
review_conversation:
Jordan Lee: Please add an integration test that simulates out-of-order chunk delivery — current unit tests look good but we need reassembly coverage.

Ava Martinez: Added e2e config and an integration case that randomizes chunk order; CI now runs it in the e2e stage.

Samir Patel: How do we ensure client_seed doesn't accidentally leak into logs? Suggest we redact the raw value in top-level request logs while preserving a stable hash for traceability.

Ava Martinez: Agreed. Implemented hashing of the seed using HMAC with the request-level secret before logging; added a unit test to assert raw value is never emitted.

Nina Chen: The structured output mapping looks correct, but can we add a note in docs about how our SDKs expose the mapped fields?

Ava Martinez: Docs updated and SDK shims expose structured_response as Response.structured in Python/TS.

Jordan Lee: Approved after changes. Samir: Approved. Nina: Approved.
ci_checks: CI pipeline: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration-e2e (pass), bench (pass), docs-build (pass). One flaky e2e run retried and passed. Total runtime: ~24m.
release_notes: Add OpenAI Responses v11 compatibility proxy: stable streaming reassembly, client_seed propagation for determinism, metadata passthrough via x-rw-user-metadata, and structured-output mapping. Feature behind openai_v11_compat flag; roll out to beta before general availability.
files_touched_excerpt: service/proxy/openai_v11_compat.go: introduced mapping table for v11 event types -> internal events; stream_reassembler.go: state machine for chunk reassembly keyed by stream_id; metadata_mapper.go: extracts user_request_metadata, validates JSON shapes, and sets x-rw-user-metadata header; sdk/python/openai_compat.py: added openai_v11 streaming client shim that re-emits reassembled events as SDK-friendly objects.
notes: Backported minimal changes to the redwood-helm-chart in a follow-up PR for Private deployments. This PR is intentionally conservative on performance-sensitive code paths and defers more aggressive optimization until telemetry from beta customers is available.
